program.major: Linguistics (Specialization in Speech and Language Sciences)

notes: 13 courses total: 12 upper-division LIGN/approved courses plus one lower-division statistics course. LIGN 110 (Phonetics) is specifically required in the core. Includes disorders, development, and neurobiology requirements plus three approved electives. Corrected: harvested data mislabeled this as '13 upper-division courses' - the statistics course is lower-division, so the upper-division count is 12.

buckets.label: Statistics course (lower-division)
buckets.note: One statistics course: COGS 14B, CSS 2, HDS 60, or PSYC 60.

buckets.label: Area breadth: one course each from two of three areas
buckets.note: One course each from TWO of three areas: Computational Linguistics; Crosslinguistic Variation; Language and Society.

buckets.label: Speech/language/hearing disorders course
buckets.note: One of LIGN 112 (Speech Sounds and Speech Disorders) or LIGN 113 (Hearing Science and Hearing Disorders).

buckets.label: Neurobiology of language course
buckets.note: One of these. Note: COGS 107C and PSYC 108 may not both be taken for credit.

buckets.label: Speech and language sciences electives
buckets.note: Three upper-division electives from the department's approved list, which the catalog describes rather than enumerates: further LIGN courses plus COGS, COMM, EDS, ETHN, PSYC, MUS 175 and SOCI 117. Those departments are matched as ranges here, so a course outside the approved list can tick this bucket — confirm your three with a Linguistics adviser. Courses already counted by another bucket are excluded. (Was two literal codes for a needed-3 bucket, which no student could ever satisfy; "SOC 117" is SOCI 117.)
